editorial: Staring deeper into space becomes a cold dread you can feel in your bones. Alien: Romulus twists the classic sci‑fi horror formula into a psychological labyrinth where isolation feels like a living entity. Its first half drifts through sluggish pacing, allowing suspense to build but at the expense of momentum. Joaquin Phoenix carries every scene with almost no dialogue, turning silent moments into a menacing presence that lingers long after the screen fades. You’ll relish it if you crave a slow‑burn, cerebral terror that drips with existential dread.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
